trend.title: Trepp: CMBS Delinquency Slips to 7.87% in October on One Loan's Cure, While Retail, Office and Multifamily Worsen
trend.scope: U.S. CMBS loans (Trepp October 2026 delinquency report, as reported by CRE Daily)
trend.metric: 7.87% overall (down 15 bps from 8.02%); retail 7.21% (+63 bps), office 12.33% (+17 bps), multifamily 8.09% (+5 bps), lodging 5.94% (-24 bps), industrial 1.10% (-4 bps)
trend.summary: Trepp's overall CMBS delinquency rate fell 15 basis points to 7.87% in October from 8.02% in September, but the improvement came largely from a single loan: a $975 million showroom portfolio loan tied to High Point and Las Vegas returned to current status. Underneath, retail posted the biggest increase, rising 63 basis points to 7.21%, office rose 17 basis points to 12.33%, still the highest of any property type, and multifamily edged up 5 basis points to 8.09%. Lodging improved to 5.94% and industrial eased to 1.10%. The largest new delinquencies were a $384.3 million Los Angeles office loan and a $210 million Bay Area apartment loan.
trend.significance: A headline decline driven by one large cure masks worsening payment performance in retail, office and multifamily, the sectors that generate most foreclosure, receivership and guaranty litigation. Newly delinquent large loans typically move to special servicing and then to default notices, receiver motions and maturity-default suits, so borrowers, guarantors and mezzanine lenders on retail and office collateral should expect more contested workouts rather than relief.
